pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word helps to show the order of steps? (1 mark)
   A. Green
   B. Table
   C. Finally
   D. Yesterday

2. Which sentence has a verb? (1 mark)
   A. Kamau washed his face.
   B. In the morning.
   C. Kamau and his face.
   D. The red bag.

3. What is role play? (1 mark)
   A. Acting out a situation
   B. Copying
   C. Drawing only
   D. Reading silently

4. What is a mosaic? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of song
   B. A long story
   C. A picture made of small pieces
   D. A heavy load

5. What should you do first when you give an instruction to a friend? (1 mark)
   A. Say all steps at once quickly
   B. Plan the steps in order
   C. Walk away
   D. Shout

6. A seller buys mangoes for 300 shillings and sells them for 450 shillings. What is the profit? (1 mark)
   A. 750 shillings
   B. 300 shillings
   C. 450 shillings
   D. 150 shillings

7. What is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. A list of names
   B. Words that tell someone what to do
   C. A story about animals
   D. A type of poem

8. Which word in this sentence is singular: The seller has an onion and two cabbages? (1 mark)
   A. onion
   B. cabbages
   C. two
   D. seller has

9. What can you use to make a poster advert? (1 mark)
   A. Only a full stop
   B. A blank page
   C. A headline, picture, adjectives, price and place
   D. Only a number

10. A sentence should begin with (1 mark)
   A. a capital letter
   B. a number
   C. a comma
   D. a small drawing

11. What is polite when you collect a song from an elder? (1 mark)
   A. Greet them and thank them at the end
   B. Take the song without asking
   C. Interrupt while they sing
   D. Refuse to listen

12. Which of these is a character? (1 mark)
   A. A cloudy afternoon
   B. Under the tree
   C. The last page
   D. A girl called Neema

13. What does an interjection show? (1 mark)
   A. A time
   B. A sudden feeling
   C. A number
   D. A place

14. Which word shows the last step in a sequence? (1 mark)
   A. Begin
   B. Next
   C. First
   D. Finally

15. What is an oral narrative? (1 mark)
   A. A drawing
   B. A written test
   C. A story told aloud
   D. A story kept secret

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Put the steps in order: (a) Finally, serve. (b) First, boil water. (c) Next, add tea leaves. (3 marks)

17. Explain how the language train game is played. (4 marks)

18. Plan a reader's theatre for a short passage about rain. Say who the roles are, how to practise and how the audience gives feedback. (5 marks)

19. Give three rules for writing clear instructions. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Finally
   Finally shows the last step.

2. A — Kamau washed his face.
   Washed is the verb.

3. A — Acting out a situation
   Role play acts a scene.

4. C — A picture made of small pieces
   A mosaic is made of small pieces of paper or seeds.

5. B — Plan the steps in order
   Planning helps to give clear instructions.

6. D — 150 shillings
   450 minus 300 is 150.

7. B — Words that tell someone what to do
   An instruction says what to do.

8. A — onion
   Onion names one thing. Cabbages is plural.

9. C — A headline, picture, adjectives, price and place
   Adverts have these parts.

10. A — a capital letter
   Every sentence starts with a capital letter.

11. A — Greet them and thank them at the end
   Good manners include greeting, listening and thanking.

12. D — A girl called Neema
   Characters are people or animals.

13. B — A sudden feeling
   Interjections show emotions.

14. D — Finally
   Finally is used for the last step.

15. C — A story told aloud
   Oral narratives are spoken stories.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: b, c, a
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct position.

17. (4 marks)
   Answer: A pupil starts with a sentence. Each next pupil continues the story with a sentence beginning with when until the story ends.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

18. (5 marks)
   Answer: Roles such as narrator, farmer, child and rain. Read your part silently three times, mark stressed words, then read aloud with expression. The audience gives one good point and one improvement.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for suitable roles, two marks for practice steps and one mark for feedback.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put steps in order, begin each step with a verb, use short sentences, one action per step, add warnings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
